title: The other half of learning: extracting lessons instead of consuming information
summary: Cris Pop argues that growth comes from actively extracting lessons from books, failures and successes, not from passively consuming information. He offers two questions and a habit of honest self-review as the difference between people who change and people who stay stuck.

principles.text: Consuming information is not learning; insights must be actively pulled out and applied.
principles.quote: But just because you’ve consumed the information doesn’t mean you’ve learned the lesson.

principles.text: Treat every experience as raw material you must work on, not something that hands you answers.
principles.quote: Every time you read something, hear something, or go through something hard, you’re being handed raw material. It’s up to you to do something with it.

principles.text: Ask two questions of every experience: what's in it for me, and what do I learn from this.
principles.quote: Two simple questions, ones that many avoid: "What's in it for me?" and "What do I learn from this?"

principles.text: When something fails, ask from ownership and insight rather than blame or self-pity.
principles.quote: This is when you stop asking from a place of blame or self-pity, and start asking from a place of ownership and insight.

principles.text: A course sells you the chance to do the work, not the transformation itself.
principles.quote: you don't pay for transformation, you pay for the chance to do the work.

principles.text: Schedule honest conversations with yourself about what you learned and how you're applying it.
principles.quote: they regularly sit down and have honest conversations with themselves about what they've learned and how they're applying it.
